R202.note: expr-eval closes the Function-constructor injection; verified with expr-eval that order.total+order.tax still evaluates (=45) while a constructor-chain call attempt fails to parse.

R203.note: Adds the missing resource-ownership check before delete; only unauthorized/non-owner callers are newly rejected, matching the CWE-862 fix.

R204.note: Replaces the evaluated string with a closure callback; identical recordReminder behavior for legitimate input, no injection surface remains.

R205.note: escapeshellarg applied to both fallback exec arguments with the same values passed through; matches the stated contract exactly.

R206.note: Replaces Runtime.exec with Files.list, eliminating the shell entirely; equivalent behavior for the normal case (output was already discarded in the original).

R207.note: Moves deletion to a CrossOriginProtection-guarded POST behind a GET confirmation page, the standard CWE-352 pattern for a state-changing GET; openly notes the one-click email link now needs a confirm click, which is the vulnerability itself being closed, not an unrelated restriction.

R208.note: Switching to Commons Net FTPClient does not close the vector: decompiled FTP.buildMessage() (verified against commons-net 3.11.1) just concatenates "RETR "+name+"\r\n" with no CR/LF filtering, so an embedded CRLF in requestedFileName still injects a second IMAP-style command exactly as before.

R209.note: StackExchange.Redis's RESP-based StringSet length-prefixes arguments, genuinely preventing the CRLF command-splitting the raw inline-protocol writer allowed.

R210.note: escapeshellarg on $host correctly neutralizes shell metacharacters while preserving the same return shape.

R211.note: Standard GET-to-POST-with-[ValidateAntiForgeryToken] fix; write-up openly flags that the (out-of-scope) confirmation view needs the antiforgery field, which is outside the single given file.

R212.note: Escaping only handles backslash/double-quote breakout; embedded CR/LF in folderName is never rejected or encoded, so the classic IMAP command-injection vector (extra command line after an early line break) is still open.

R213.note: Canonicalizes and checks containment with a separator-aware prefix check, the correct robust pattern; the redundant ".." prefix pre-check is backstopped by the authoritative containment check so it doesn't materially restrict legitimate input.

R214.note: Standard parameterized query via SqlCommand.Parameters; same results for legitimate input, no behavior change.

R215.note: Verified by building and running the fix against a live Kestrel host: antiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync succeeds with the default "RequestVerificationToken" header plus matching cookie, and correctly rejects missing/invalid tokens, so the JSON-bound minimal API endpoint is genuinely protected without extra configuration.

R216.note: Build FAILs (missing System.Data using for SqlDbType), scored 0 on fix_quality per rubric; the parameterization design itself would have preserved the contract (apostrophes still matched literally) had it compiled.
